spec_determinacy.method: Static: each audited assertion of a test (error-detail/message equality, containment or pattern; byte-level stdout comparison) is classified against the text of its origin checkpoint's specification and every earlier one (rules below). Dynamic: reference k and spec-conformant variants of it (variants below) are graded at step k; a case is sensitive to a variant when it passes on the reference and not on the variant. A case is flagged when its test has an undetermined assertion of the kind a variant it is sensitive to rewrites.

rules.content-stated: determined: a paragraph states what the category's detail contains
rules.content-unstated: undetermined: error text must contain an input value or match a pattern; no paragraph states what the category's detail contains
rules.exact-stated: determined: a paragraph states the exact content of the category's detail
rules.exact-unstated: undetermined: error text must equal an input value; no paragraph states exact content
rules.format-stated: determined: the specification names an output byte format
rules.format-unstated: undetermined: stdout compared byte for byte; no byte format stated
rules.literal-in-spec: determined: the asserted literal occurs in the specification text
rules.wording-unstated: undetermined: an error-text literal in neither the specification nor the test's inputs

variants.neutral_error_text: every error's human-readable text (an error object's detail or message) replaced by 'request rejected'; category, exit code and format kept
variants.reformatted_json: JSON stdout re-serialised with two-space indentation and a trailing newline; value and key order kept
